mcqs.question: What is the definition of a crystal lattice?

options.A: A regular three-dimensional arrangement of atoms, ions or molecules in a solid.
options.B: The smallest repeating unit in a crystal.

mcqs.answer: A regular three-dimensional arrangement of atoms, ions or molecules in a solid.
mcqs.explanation: A crystal lattice is the orderly, three‑dimensional pattern in which the constituent particles (atoms, ions or molecules) are arranged throughout a solid. Option B describes a unit cell, not the lattice itself. Options C and D are unrelated concepts.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines a unit cell in a crystal lattice?

options.A: The smallest repeating three‑dimensional portion of the lattice that, when stacked, recreates the whole crystal.
options.B: A single atom in the crystal.
options.C: The outermost layer of a crystal.
options.D: A defect in the crystal structure.

mcqs.answer: The smallest repeating three‑dimensional portion of the lattice that, when stacked, recreates the whole crystal.
mcqs.explanation: A unit cell is the fundamental building block of a crystal lattice; repeating it in three dimensions generates the entire crystal. Options B, C, and D describe other entities, not the unit cell.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify primitive and centred unit cells
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a primitive unit cell from a centred unit cell?

options.A: A primitive cell contains only one lattice point per cell, whereas a centred cell has additional lattice points at its centre or faces.
options.B: A primitive cell is larger than a centred cell.
options.C: A centred cell has no lattice points at the corners.
options.D: Both have the same number of lattice points.

mcqs.answer: A primitive cell contains only one lattice point per cell, whereas a centred cell has additional lattice points at its centre or faces.
mcqs.explanation: In a primitive cell the lattice points are only at the corners, giving one lattice point per cell. Centred cells (body‑centred, face‑centred, etc.) have extra points inside the cell, increasing the effective lattice points. Options B, C, and D are incorrect descriptions.

mcqs.question: In a face‑centered cubic (fcc) lattice, what is the coordination number of each ion?
mcqs.explanation: In an fcc lattice each ion touches 12 nearest neighbours, giving a coordination number of 12. Coordination numbers of 8, 6, and 4 correspond to body‑centred cubic, simple cubic, and tetrahedral arrangements respectively.

mcqs.question: Why does sodium chloride (NaCl) have a relatively high melting point?

options.A: Because of its strong ionic lattice with a high coordination number.
options.C: Because it forms a covalent network structure.
options.D: Because of extensive hydrogen bonding between ions.

mcqs.answer: Because of its strong ionic lattice with a high coordination number.
mcqs.explanation: NaCl consists of a three‑dimensional ionic lattice where each Na⁺ is surrounded by six Cl⁻ ions (and vice‑versa). The strong electrostatic attraction and high coordination number require a large amount of energy to break, resulting in a high melting point. Options B, C, and D describe bonding types not present in NaCl.

mcqs.question: A student observes that a mineral forms identical shapes in all directions of the crystal. Which concept best explains this observation?

options.A: Crystal lattice – regular repetition of a basic structural unit
options.C: Molecular orbital theory governing electronic transitions

mcqs.answer: Crystal lattice – regular repetition of a basic structural unit
mcqs.explanation: The identical shapes arise because the mineral’s particles are arranged in a crystal lattice, where a basic structural unit repeats periodically in three dimensions. An amorphous solid (B) lacks such order, while C and D are unrelated to crystal shape.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about a unit cell is FALSE?

options.A: A unit cell is the smallest repeating unit that can build the entire crystal.
options.B: A unit cell must contain exactly one atom.
options.C: The shape of a unit cell can be cubic, tetragonal, orthorhombic, etc.
options.D: Unit cells can be primitive or centred.

mcqs.answer: A unit cell must contain exactly one atom.
mcqs.explanation: A unit cell may contain a fraction of atoms at its corners, faces, edges, or centre; the total contribution adds up to one lattice point for a primitive cell, but the actual number of atoms can be more than one. Therefore statement B is false. Statements A, C, and D are correct descriptions of unit cells.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify primitive and centred unit cells
mcqs.question: If a crystal lattice has lattice points at each corner and one at the centre of the cube, what type of unit cell does it represent?

options.A: Body‑centred cubic (BCC) – a centred unit cell
options.B: Simple cubic – a primitive unit cell
options.C: Face‑centred cubic – a primitive unit cell

mcqs.answer: Body‑centred cubic (BCC) – a centred unit cell
mcqs.explanation: A lattice with points at all eight corners and an additional point at the centre of the cube is characteristic of a body‑centred cubic (BCC) lattice, which is a centred unit cell. Simple cubic lacks the centre point, face‑centred cubic has points at each face centre, and hexagonal is a different lattice system.
